**Resumo.** Este artigo pergunta se modelos de sobrevivência, de aprendizado de máquina e de
aprendizado profundo antecipam a recuperação judicial ou extrajudicial de companhias abertas
brasileiras não financeiras melhor do que os escores contábeis clássicos, e se sinais de estresse
lidos por modelos de linguagem nos fatos relevantes acrescentam informação. A base de eventos vem
de registros públicos da CVM, datados pelo que era conhecido em cada data; oito modelos são
comparados num único teste fora do tempo, a partir de 2020, com intervalos por bootstrap agrupado
por empresa. Fora do tempo, os modelos de árvores chegam a uma AUC de cerca de
`{python} fmt(N['test_h1'].set_index('model').loc[['xgb_pd12', 'xgb_cox', 'rsf'], 'auc'].mean(), 2).replace('.', ',')`
na PD de 12 meses, contra
`{python} fmt(N['test_h1'].set_index('model').at['altman', 'auc'], 2).replace('.', ',')` do escore
de Altman e
`{python} fmt(N['test_h1'].set_index('model').at['logit_hazard', 'auc'], 2).replace('.', ',')` do logit
de risco. Os modelos de árvores superam o escore de Altman mesmo quando as empresas são reamostradas
inteiras, mas nesse teste nenhum se separa do logit de risco; nenhum modelo é bem calibrado em todos
os prazos. Nem o teste pré-registrado nem a rodada exploratória que mantém os sinais mais raros
encontram ganho nos sinais lidos pelos modelos de linguagem. Uma
revisão sistemática (PRISMA 2020) mostra as lacunas que o estudo ocupa. Por fim,
um parecer de crédito gerado por agentes, com trava numérica, e um desenho de serviço de
monitoramento alinhado à Resolução CMN 4.966/2021.

**Correction (23 November 2026).** An independent review of the code, after the first version
was published, found errors that changed published results. The going-concern flag also matched
the auditor-responsibility paragraph that every audit opinion carries since 2016, so it was set
for most filings from then on, including the memo on Casas Bahia, which stated a going-concern
paragraph that the auditor's report did not contain. The calibration sample (H3) kept rows whose
window was still open only when they had ended in a filing, which overstated the observed rates
and produced the first version's finding that the models underestimate the long-horizon rate.
Episodes still open in the registry were closed at their last filing, and the trailing twelve
months were wrong for fiscal years ending in March. The code was corrected, each fix with a test,
and the whole test was run again; the hypotheses, models, split and primary test did not change.
The corrections are listed in `PREREGISTRATION.md`, and every number in this version comes from
the corrected run. Comparisons now also report a test that resamples firms whole, beside DeLong's.
Three conclusions of the first version changed: in the corrected run the hazard logit is a much
stronger benchmark (AUC 0.816, against 0.758 before), and no model's edge over it survives the
firm-resampled test;
most models now overestimate the long-horizon rate rather than underestimate it; and the gain the
exploratory signal test suggested (an AUC of 0.783) does not appear in the corrected run.

# Introduction

Judicial recovery filings by large Brazilian listed companies have become frequent enough to
matter for every lender, supplier and bond investor in the country. Oi filed in
`{python} event_date(11312)` and again in `{python} event_date(11312, 1)`; Americanas in
`{python} event_date(20990)`, after an accounting inconsistency was disclosed; Light in
`{python} event_date(19879)`. Each case was followed by losses for banks, bondholders and the
suppliers who had sold on credit. The question a credit committee asks after each of them is the
same: was there anything in the public record, a year earlier, that should have changed the
decision?

The academic literature offers two traditions to answer it. Accounting scores, from
@beaver1966, @altman1968 and @ohlson1980 to the emerging-market version of @altman2005, summarise
the balance sheet in one number. Hazard models, introduced to the field by @shumway2001 and
extended by @chava2004, @duffie2007 and @campbell2008, treat default as an event in time and use
every firm-year, not one snapshot per firm. Since then, machine learning
[@barboza2017; @jones2017; @lessmann2015] and deep learning [@mai2019] have been compared with
both, and text from filings has entered as a predictor [@loughran2011; @mai2019]. Large language
models now make it cheap to read every filing a company sends to its regulator
[@huang2023; @kim2024; @lopezlira2023].

Three things are missing for Brazil, and they are the subject of this paper. First, there is no
public, point-in-time event base of judicial and out-of-court recoveries of listed firms; studies
use the current registry status, which mixes dates and loses firms that left the market. Second,
survival, tree-based and neural models have not been compared on the same Brazilian panel and the
same out-of-time test. Third, no study we found measures, with a test fixed in advance, whether
signals read by language models from material-fact filings improve on accounting and
macroeconomic information.

We state three hypotheses. H1: survival and machine learning models discriminate better, out of
time, than the Altman score and the discrete-time logit. H2: distress signals read by a language
model from material facts improve the discrimination of the 12-month probability of default (PD).
H3: survival models give better calibrated PD term structures at 12, 24 and 36 months, which is
what lifetime expected loss requires. The primary test of H2 was fixed before the test period was
opened (Section 5.5).

The paper is organised as follows. Section 2 summarises the regulatory frame. Section 3 reports
the systematic review and the gaps it shows. Section 4 describes the data and the event base,
Section 5 the method, and Section 6 the results. Section 7 presents the agentic credit memo and
Section 8 the corporate solution. Section 9 lists the limitations and Section 10 concludes.

# Regulatory context

CMN Resolution 4,966 of 25 November 2021 [@cmn4966] moved Brazilian financial institutions to an
expected-loss model for credit, with most of its provisions in force from 1 January 2025. Article
37 allocates each financial instrument to one of three stages: instruments without a significant
increase in credit risk since origination (first stage), instruments whose credit risk has
increased significantly (second stage), and instruments with a credit recovery problem (third
stage). Under Article 47, the provision for the first stage is the expected loss over the next 12
months; for the second stage it is the expected loss over the whole expected term of the
instrument. Article 40 asks the probability of default to consider the expected term and
"reasonable and justifiable forecasts" of economic conditions.

Two requirements follow for a corporate credit model. It must produce a term structure of default
probabilities, not a single score, and it must detect a significant increase in credit risk early
enough to move an exposure from the first to the second stage. Survival models produce the first
by construction; the second is the early-warning problem this paper studies.

# Systematic review

## Protocol and search

The review follows PRISMA 2020 [@page2021]. The protocol (`slr/protocol.md`) was written and
committed before the search ran, and two dated amendments record the changes made while it ran.
Three strands were searched for 2000 to 2026: (a) corporate default, bankruptcy or financial
distress prediction with survival, machine learning or neural models; (b) text, natural language
processing or large language models applied to credit risk or distress; (c) Brazilian evidence on
bankruptcy, insolvency or judicial recovery. The protocol named OpenAlex as the source; when its
anonymous quota was exhausted on the day of the search, the same strings were run on the Semantic
Scholar bulk search (Amendment 1). Records were deduplicated by DOI and by normalised title.

```{python}
#| output: asis
P = N["prisma"]
print(
    f"The search returned {fmt(P['identified'])} records; {fmt(P['duplicates_removed'])} duplicates "
    f"were removed and {fmt(P['screened'])} titles and abstracts were screened."
)
```

## Screening and extraction

Titles and abstracts were screened against written criteria by two open-weight language models
working independently (Gemma 4 26B and Gemma 4 31B, temperature zero). A record entered the review
when either model included it (Amendment 2); this inclusive rule favours recall at the screening
stage, where a false exclusion cannot be recovered later.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(
    f"The two screeners agreed on {fmt(P['agreement'], 1, pct=True)} of the records (Cohen's kappa "
    f"{fmt(P['kappa_screeners'], 2)}, [@cohen1960]). {fmt(P['excluded_title_abstract'])} records were "
    f"excluded and {fmt(P['included'])} included, of which {fmt(P['full_text_open_access'])} have an "
    f"open-access full text."
)
```

Every included study was coded from its abstract: model families, validation design, country,
unit of analysis, use of text and of language models, and number of events. A core of studies was
then read in full. The core was drawn by stratum, so that each strand the gaps are about (survival
models, deep learning, text and language models, Brazil, out-of-time validation) has up to ten
studies read in depth, and was filled with the most cited studies per year since publication.
Full texts were taken only from open-access copies; publisher sites that refuse automated requests
were not worked around, and the next study in the stratum took the place of one that could not be
retrieved.

```{python}
#| output: asis
C = N["core"]
if C:
    print(f"Of {fmt(C['tried'])} open-access studies tried, {fmt(C['full_text'])} gave a full text; "
          f"the core holds {fmt(C['core'])} studies, {fmt(C['read_ok'])} of them read and coded.")
else:
    print(fmt(None))
```

# Data

## Sources

All data are public. Financial statements come from the quarterly (ITR, 2011 to 2026) and annual
(DFP, 2010 to 2026) filings in the CVM open-data portal [@cvmdados], using consolidated accounts and
individual accounts when no consolidated set exists. Each filing carries its delivery date to the
regulator, which is the date the information becomes available to the model; a restated filing
counts only from its own delivery date. The auditor's report attached to each filing is read for
the going-concern paragraph. Event filings (IPE, 2003 to 2026) give the material facts and the
category of documents filed by companies in judicial or out-of-court recovery. Macroeconomic
series come from the Central Bank's time-series system [@bcbsgs]: the Selic rate, 12-month IPCA
inflation, the IBC-Br activity index, unemployment, the corporate non-performing-loan ratio over
90 days and the average lending spread, each lagged by its publication delay.

# Method

## Predictors

Accounting variables follow the literature [@altman1968; @ohlson1980; @shumway2001;
@campbell2008]: working capital, retained earnings and EBIT over total assets, equity over total
liabilities, leverage, current ratio, cash over assets, interest coverage, margin, revenue growth,
size (assets deflated by IPCA), a negative-equity flag and a flag for a loss in the last four
quarters. Flows are trailing twelve months. Disclosure behaviour adds the filing delay, the number
of restatements in the last four quarters, the age of the latest information, the going-concern
flag and an indicator of a previous recovery. The going-concern flag comes from a text rule that
accepts only a statement of material uncertainty about the filer, such as the section the auditor
opens under that heading; the conditional sentence about the auditor's responsibilities, present
in every opinion since the 2016 reports, does not set it. Fiscal years that end in a month other
than December are handled when flows are summed over twelve months. The six
macroeconomic series complete the base set.

## Models

Eight models are fitted on the same rows and the same predictors: the @altman2005 score with a
logistic calibration; a discrete-time hazard logit [@shumway2001] with an L2 penalty chosen by
temporal cross-validation; a Cox model [@cox1972] on landmark rows with a Breslow baseline
[@breslow1974]; an XGBoost classifier of the 12-month PD and an XGBoost survival model with the Cox
objective [@chen2016]; a random survival forest [@ishwaran2008]; DeepSurv [@katzman2018]; and
DeepHit [@lee2018]. Survival models are fitted on stacked landmarks: each firm-quarter starts a
follow-up that ends at the event, at the firm's exit or at 36 months, which gives PD curves at 12,
24 and 36 months for every row. Hyper-parameters were set by a split inside the training years
(fit to 2015, validate on 2017 and 2018); the test period was not used.

## Evaluation

For the 12-month PD we report the area under the ROC curve (AUC), the area under the
precision-recall curve, the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic, the Brier score and the calibration
intercept and slope [@vancalster2019]. For the term structure we report Harrell's [@harrell1982]
and Uno's [@uno2011] concordance, time-dependent AUC at 12, 24 and 35 months and the integrated
Brier score [@graf1999]. Intervals are 95% percentiles of a bootstrap that resamples firms, not
rows, because rows of one firm are dependent. Differences in AUC are tested with DeLong's method
[@delong1988], with Holm's correction [@holm1979] for the secondary comparisons. DeLong's test
treats rows as independent; since the events come from a few dozen firms, every comparison also
reports a paired bootstrap that resamples firms whole and refits nothing, with its one-sided
p-value and 95% interval for the difference. Where the two disagree, the text says so.

## Language-model signals

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(
    f"The subject line of each of the {fmt(N.get('signal_docs'))} material facts filed by the firms in "
    f"the panel since 2010 is classified into eleven categories of distress: debt restructuring, "
    f"covenant breach or waiver, missed payment, asset sale for liquidity, emergency capital, "
    f"going-concern doubt, change of chief executive or chief financial officer, rating downgrade, the "
    f"company's own recovery, a subsidiary's recovery, and sanction. The company's registered name and its "
    f"tax number are masked before the text reaches the model, so that the model's memory of what later "
    f"happened to a known company is less likely to leak into the label; trade names that differ from the "
    f"registered name are not masked. Announcements of the company's own "
    f"recovery are kept for auditing the event base but never used as a predictor. A document enters the "
    f"panel only from its delivery date; the features are counts of each category in the 4 and 12 months "
    f"before the quarter. {fmt(N.get('signal_any'))} documents carry at least one signal."
)
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
_K, _L = N["signals_kappa"], N["subject_loss"]
print(f"Reliability is measured two ways. A second model reads a random subsample of "
      f"{fmt(next(iter(_K.values()))['n']) if _K else fmt(None)} documents and agreement is reported per category "
      f"as Cohen's kappa [@cohen1960], next to the number of flags from each reader, since on a rare category a few "
      f"extra flags move kappa a long way. And {fmt(_L['sample']) if _L else fmt(None)} documents drawn at random "
      f"are read in full, to measure what the subject line misses.")
```

## Pre-registered test of H2

The primary test of H2 was fixed before the test period was opened: the discrete-time hazard
logit with and without the language-model signals, compared by the AUC of the 12-month PD on the
out-of-time test, with a one-sided DeLong test at the 5% level. All other models, metrics and
horizons are secondary and carry Holm's correction. The going-concern flag from the text rule
stays in the baseline, so that the treated arm adds only what the language model reads.

The second reader's labels came in after the registration and before the test was opened. They
led to one amendment, committed with them: a secondary version of the H2 test in which the treated
arm keeps only the categories where the two readers reach a kappa of 0.60, the lower edge of what
@landis1977 call substantial agreement. The threshold was set after the agreement was seen; the
primary test is unchanged. A second amendment, also before the test was opened, replaced the
review of the event list by hand with the second reader's rule of @sec-events, so that the event
base can be rebuilt by anyone from the cached answers.

# Results

## Discrimination and calibration (H1, H3)

```{python}
#| output: asis
H1, DL, H3 = N["test_h1"], N["test_delong"], N["test_h3"]
nm = lambda m: MODEL_NAMES.get(m, m)  # noqa: E731
words = lambda ms: ", ".join(nm(m) for m in ms[:-1]) + (" and " if len(ms) > 1 else "") + nm(ms[-1])  # noqa: E731
if H1 is not None:
    r = H1.set_index("model")
    trees = [m for m in ("xgb_cox", "xgb_pd12", "rsf") if m in r.index]
    def wins(col):
        b = DL[DL[col] < 0.05]
        return {m: set(b.loc[b["model"] == m, "versus"]) for m in r.index}

    def groups(won):
        both = [m for m in r.index if {"altman", "logit_hazard"} <= won[m]]
        only_logit = [m for m in r.index if m not in both and "logit_hazard" in won[m]]
        only_altman = [m for m in r.index if m not in both and "altman" in won[m]]
        neither = [m for m in r.index if m not in both + only_logit + only_altman + ["altman", "logit_hazard"]]
        return both, only_logit, only_altman, neither

    def says(won):
        both, only_logit, only_altman, neither = groups(won)
        parts = [f"{words(both)} beat{'s' if len(both) == 1 else ''} both benchmarks"] if both else []
        parts += [f"{words(g)} beat{'s' if len(g) == 1 else ''} {what}" for g, what in
                  ((only_logit, "the logit only"), (only_altman, "the Altman score only"), (neither, "neither")) if g]
        return "; ".join(parts)

    best = r["auc"].sort_values(ascending=False).index
    lead = [m for m in best[:3]]
    both_d, both_c = groups(wins("p_holm"))[0], groups(wins("p_cluster_holm"))[0]
    text = (f"On the {fmt(int(r['n'].iloc[0]))} test firm-quarters whose 12-month window is observed "
            f"({fmt(int(r['events'].iloc[0]))} of them followed by a filing within 12 months), the highest AUCs are: "
            + "; ".join(f"{nm(m)} {fmt(r.at[m, 'auc'], 3)} [{fmt(r.at[m, 'auc_lo'], 3)}, {fmt(r.at[m, 'auc_hi'], 3)}]"
                        for m in lead)
            + f"; against {fmt(r.at['altman', 'auc'], 3)} for the Altman score and "
            f"{fmt(r.at['logit_hazard', 'auc'], 3)} for the hazard logit (@tbl-h1). With DeLong's test and Holm's "
            f"correction (@tbl-delong), {says(wins('p_holm'))}. With the firm-clustered test, {says(wins('p_cluster_holm'))}.")
    ens = [m for m in trees if m in both_c]
    text += (f" H1 holds for {words(ens)} under both tests." if ens else
             " No model beats both benchmarks under the firm-clustered test, so H1 is not established once the "
             "dependence of a firm's quarters is taken into account.")
    text += " The intervals overlap enough that the order among the leading models is not established."
    print(text)
if H3 is not None:
    h = H3.set_index(["model", "horizon"])
    obs = {k: H3.loc[H3["horizon"] == k, "observed"].iloc[0] for k in (12, 24, 36)}
    m12 = H3[H3["horizon"] == 12].set_index("model")["mean_pd"]
    m36 = H3[H3["horizon"] == 36].set_index("model")["mean_pd"]
    br36 = H3[H3["horizon"] == 36].set_index("model")["brier"]
    sl = H3.set_index(["model", "horizon"])["calib_slope"]
    b36 = br36.idxmin()
    close = lambda k: H3[H3["horizon"] == k].assign(gap=lambda d: (d["mean_pd"] - d["observed"]).abs()).nsmallest(2, "gap")  # noqa: E731
    over = [m for m in m36.index if m36[m] > obs[36]]
    under = [m for m in m36.index if m36[m] <= obs[36]]
    flat = [m for m in sl.index.get_level_values(0).unique() if (sl.loc[m] < 1).all()]
    steep = [m for m in sl.index.get_level_values(0).unique() if (sl.loc[m] > 1).all()]
    surv = [m for m in ("cox", "xgb_cox", "rsf", "deepsurv", "deephit") if m in br36.index]
    better = [m for m in surv if br36[m] < br36["logit_hazard"]]
    side = (f"{words(over)} overestimate{'s' if len(over) == 1 else ''} it" if over else "") + \
           ("; " if over and under else "") + \
           (f"{words(under)} underestimate{'s' if len(under) == 1 else ''} it" if under else "")
    print(f"\n\nObserved rates are measured on the rows whose window has closed by the end of the data, chosen "
          f"by date alone (@tbl-h3). At 12 months the observed rate is {fmt(obs[12], 2, pct=True)} and the mean PD "
          f"ranges from {fmt(m12.min(), 2, pct=True)} ({nm(m12.idxmin())}) to {fmt(m12.max(), 2, pct=True)} "
          f"({nm(m12.idxmax())}); {words(list(close(12)['model']))} come closest. At 36 months the observed rate is "
          f"{fmt(obs[36], 1, pct=True)}: {side}; {words(list(close(36)['model']))} come closest."
          + (f" Calibration slopes are below one at every horizon for {words(flat)}, so their PDs spread more than the "
             f"outcomes" if flat else "")
          + (f"{'; ' if flat else ' Calibration slopes are '}above one at every horizon for {words(steep)}, whose PDs "
             f"are too compressed" if steep else "") + ". "
          f"{nm(b36)} has the lowest Brier score at 36 months, and {spell(len(better))} of the {spell(len(surv))} "
          f"survival models have a lower 36-month Brier score than the hazard logit. "
          + ("H3 holds in part: " if 0 < len(better) < len(surv) else ("H3 holds: " if better else "H3 does not hold: "))
          + "the level of every curve has to be checked against the lender's own defaults before it feeds a "
          "lifetime provision.")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
```

```{python}
if K:

    n_more = sum(v["primary"] > v["secondary"] for v in K.values())
    print(f"On the {fmt(next(iter(K.values()))['n'])} subjects both models read, kappa ranges from "

          f"subjects carry no signal at all, so kappa is the informative figure. The first reader flags more "
          f"often than the second in {fmt(n_more)} of the {fmt(len(K))} categories. Kappa falls below 0.60 in "

L = N["subject_loss"]
if L:

    ch = L["checks"]
    print(f" In the full-text sample ({fmt(L['read'])} documents read), the subject line finds "
          f"{fmt(a['both'])} of the {fmt(a['full_text'])} documents that carry a signal in the full text "

          f"({fmt(lo['debt_restructuring']['both'])} of {fmt(lo['debt_restructuring']['full_text'])}). Flags of the "
          f"company's own recovery in the full text ({fmt(ch['own_recovery_full_text'])}) come almost all "
          f"({fmt(ch['own_recovery_full_text_inside_open_episode'])}) from firms already in recovery, whose filings "
          f"restate that status. Since the subject line keeps most of the signal, the panel uses subjects; the "
          f"result for debt renegotiation is a limitation of H2 and the reason the monitor of Section 8 reads "
          f"whole documents.")
H2, H2R, H2X, AB = N["test_h2"], N["test_h2_reliable"], N["test_h2_exploratory"], N["test_h2_ablation"]
if H2:
    txt = (f"\n\nThe pre-registered test does not support H2. On the {fmt(H2['n'])} test rows "

    if H2R:

                f"{fmt(H2R['auc_signals'], 3)} (p = {fmt(H2R['p_one_sided'], 2)}; resampling firms, "

    if H2X:
        flat = [CATEGORY_NAMES[c[4:-4]].lower() for c in H2X["flat_after_winsorising"]]
        txt += (f" One flaw lies in the preprocessing, which was fixed with the rest of the code before the "
                f"registration: every predictor is winsorised at the 1st and 99th percentiles of the training rows, "
                f"and {spell(len(flat))} signal counts ({', '.join(flat[:-1])} and {flat[-1]}) are non-zero in fewer "
                f"than 1% of those rows, so winsorising turned them into constant zeros and the registered tests ran "
                f"without them. The tests were repeated with the signal counts left unclipped. That run was decided "
                f"after the test period was opened and is exploratory: it gives an AUC of "
                f"{fmt(H2X['all']['auc_signals'], 3)} with all signals (DeLong p = {fmt(H2X['all']['p_one_sided'], 2)}; "

    if AB is not None:
        sec = AB[(AB["role"] == "secondary") & (AB["model"] != "altman")]  # Altman's score has fixed inputs
        txt += (f" Across the other {spell(len(sec))} models that take the signals, adding them changes the AUC by between "
                f"{fmt(sec['auc_diff'].min(), 3)} and {fmt(sec['auc_diff'].max(), 3)}, and "
                + (lambda k: "none of the changes is" if k == 0 else f"{spell(k)} of the changes {'is' if k == 1 else 'are'}")(
                    int((sec["p_holm"] < 0.05).sum()))
                + " significant after Holm's correction (@tbl-ablation).")
    print(txt)
else:
    print("\n\n" + fmt(None))
```

```{python}
          f"a lot (@tbl-rolling).")
    piv = RR.pivot_table(index="model", columns="year", values="auc").reindex(order.index)
    piv.insert(0, "Model", [nm(m) for m in piv.index])
    piv.columns = [str(c) for c in piv.columns]
    print("\n\n: AUC of the 12-month PD by test year, with an annual refit on a moving origin. {#tbl-rolling}\n")
    print(table(piv.reset_index(drop=True)))
```

# Agentic credit memo

The product layer turns the models into a credit memo for a committee. An orchestrator calls
deterministic tools (the firm's panel row, its PD curve, the main drivers, the macroeconomic
context and the material facts delivered before the memo date) and two language-model subagents: a
reader, which summarises the recent filings, and a writer, which drafts the memo. A deterministic
critic then checks every number and every date in the draft against the values the tools returned;
a memo with a number or a year that no tool produced is blocked. Language models are known to
state plausible facts that no source supports [@ji2023]; the critic does not ask the model to
behave, it rejects any figure without a source. It does not check that a figure sits in the right
place: a memo that swapped two values the tools did return, such as the 12- and 36-month PDs,
would pass.

```{python}
#| output: asis
```

# Corporate solution

The design, called here a corporate credit monitor, follows from the regulatory frame and from what
the experiment shows. It watches the CVM filings of the firms in a client's portfolio every day,
recomputes a monthly PD curve per firm, raises an alert when a distress signal appears or the PD
crosses a threshold set by the client's credit policy, and drafts a memo with the agentic layer for
the credit committee. Every number in a memo traces back to a filing or a model output. It runs in
the client's environment, and the decision stays with people.

The monitor maps directly onto Resolution 4,966: the 12-month PD feeds first-stage provisions, the
36-month curve the lifetime loss of the second stage, and the alerts are candidates for the
significant-increase-in-credit-risk test that moves an exposure between them. A typical engagement
starts with a diagnosis of the client's portfolio and data, runs a pilot of six to eight weeks on
that portfolio, and continues with monthly monitoring.

# Limitations

The number of events is small, so intervals are wide and the comparison rests on the intervals,
not on the ranking. Market data (share prices, credit spreads) were left out because no public,
stable source covers the whole panel. The event base depends on how firms describe their own
filings; the list was checked by a second language model under a fixed rule rather than by hand,
so some events may still carry a wrong date or belong to another company of the group, and a
narrow definition (judicial recovery and bankruptcy only) is reported as a robustness check. No
human labels were collected for the signals: the two models agree on most categories, but how
close either comes to a human reading is not measured. Screening and extraction in the review were
done by language models; their agreement is reported, but no human screened the full set, and
studies without an open-access text enter only through their abstracts. The signals are read from
subject lines; the full-text sample measures what that costs. The registered preprocessing erased
the rarest signal counts, so the test of H2 that keeps them is exploratory, whatever it shows. The memos on past cases name firms whose stories are public, and the model
that writes them may know how those stories ended. Trade names that differ from a company's
registered name are not masked in the signal prompts. The corrections listed at the top of the
paper were made after the test period was opened; they fix code that did not do what the
registration describes, and the hypotheses, models and primary test did not change, but a reader
should weigh results obtained after an opening accordingly.

# Conclusion

```{python}
    r = H1.set_index("model")
    ens = r.loc[["xgb_pd12", "xgb_cox", "rsf"], "auc"]
    yrs = RR.pivot_table(index="model", columns="year", values="auc") if RR is not None else None
    wins = int((yrs.loc["xgb_cox"] > yrs.loc["altman"]).sum()) if yrs is not None else None
    hi = max(M, key=lambda m: m["pd12"]) if M else None
    C = N["claims"]
    ens_a = [m for m in ("xgb_pd12", "xgb_cox", "rsf") if m in C["beats_altman_c"]]
    ens_l = [m for m in ("xgb_pd12", "xgb_cox", "rsf") if m in C["beats_logit_c"]]
    rel = ("tree ensembles do it better than both benchmarks the literature uses, the accounting score and the "
           "hazard logit" if ens_a and ens_l else
           "tree ensembles do it better than the accounting score, while their edge over a well-specified hazard "
           "logit is not significant once a firm's quarters are resampled together" if ens_a else
           "the differences among models are within what a panel of this size can tell apart")
    print(
        f"Public filings are enough to rank Brazilian listed companies by their risk of judicial or "
        f"out-of-court recovery a year ahead, and {rel}: an out-of-time AUC between {fmt(ens.min(), 3)} and "
        f"{fmt(ens.max(), 3)} for the ensembles, against {fmt(r.at['altman', 'auc'], 3)} for the Altman score and "
        f"{fmt(r.at['logit_hazard', 'auc'], 3)} for the hazard logit. The ensembles stay ahead of the Altman score "
        f"under the narrow event definition"
        + (f" and in {spell(wins)} of the {spell(yrs.shape[1])} years of the moving-origin refit" if wins is not None else "")
        + ". The levels are another matter: no model is calibrated at every horizon, so a lender that uses these "
        "curves for lifetime provisions under Resolution 4,966 has to recalibrate them on its own portfolio.\n\n"
        + (f"Language models did not add to accounting data in this test. The test registered in advance finds no "
           f"gain (AUC {fmt(H2['auc_signals'], 3)} with the signals, {fmt(H2['auc_base'], 3)} without), and neither "
           f"does the exploratory rerun that keeps the rarest signals ({fmt(H2X['all']['auc_signals'], 3)}). Signals "
           f"read from subject lines may be too thin; whole documents are the next thing to test."
           if C["exploratory_gain"] is False else
           f"Whether language models add to accounting data is not settled. The test registered in advance says no "
           f"(AUC {fmt(H2['auc_signals'], 3)} with the signals, {fmt(H2['auc_base'], 3)} without). The same test with "
           f"the rarest signals kept gives {fmt(H2X['all']['auc_signals'], 3)}, but that analysis came after the "
           f"test was opened and needs a new test period before it counts.")
        + (f" The memos on past cases show what a monitor can and cannot do. A year before the filing, the hazard "
           f"logit's highest PD among them was {fmt(hi['pd12'], 1, pct=True)}, {fmt(hi['pd12'] / N['train_rate12'], 1)} "
           f"times the average 12-month rate; it could not see Americanas, whose problem sat in accounts that no "
           f"outside model could read." if hi else "")
        + "\n\nThe monitor of the previous section follows from these results: rank the portfolio with a tree "
        "ensemble, recalibrate the curves on the client's own defaults, read whole filings rather than subject "
        "lines, and let a deterministic critic check every number a language model writes."
    )
else:
    print(fmt(None))
```

# Data and code availability {.unnumbered}

Code, derived data, the cached answers of every language-model call, tests and the review's records
are in the public repository `rhozon/corporate-credit-early-warning`. Raw CVM and Central Bank files
are downloaded by the code. Language models were used as instruments of the method, as described in
Sections 3 to 5 and 7; the models, versions and settings are recorded in the repository.
